issue.title: Epic phase agents inherit the live epic-launch monitor's SASE_MONITOR_ID, so their sase tool runs record as monitor-owned with no compact output or retained logs
issue.description:
An agent launched by a monitored command, such as an epic launch (`sase bead work <plan>` runs
as a monitor), inherits that monitor's `SASE_MONITOR_ID` / `SASE_MONITOR_ARTIFACTS_DIR`.
`sase.tool.ownership.resolve_ownership` treats the id as stale only after the monitor has
settled (`done.json`). While the epic-launch monitor is still running, which is the whole
life of its phase agents, every `sase tool run` by a phase agent is recorded as
**monitor-owned**. It gets `owns_output=False`, so the agent gets no compact output (full
passthrough into its context), no stdout/stderr is retained (`sase tool show RUN -l` has
nothing to replay), and the run is attributed to an owner that never captured its output.

Evidence from athena's ledger (2026-09-22): 4 `check` runs by agent `sase-135.7` have
`owner_kind=monitor`, `owner_id=136v0dbr3pv1`. That is `0nm--mon`, the monitor running
`sase bead work .../tool_e1_named_tools.md`. Their `logs` contain only an `events_path`, with
no stdout/stderr paths.

Root cause: the agent-spawn env boundary scrubs `SASE_AGENT*` (`scrub_agent_identity_env`),
but not executor-ownership variables (`SASE_MONITOR_ID`, `SASE_MONITOR_ARTIFACTS_DIR`,
`SASE_PROC_*`, `SASE_TOOL_RUN_ID`, `SASE_TOOL_RUN_EVENTS`). An agent is a new ownership root:
nothing its own shell runs is captured by the ancestor monitor. The same leak would make any
agent launched inside a `sase tool run` record its runs as children of that ancestor run
(`_parent_exists` checks existence, not liveness).

Fix direction: scrub executor-ownership variables at agent launch (the epic launcher reads
`SASE_MONITOR_ARTIFACTS_DIR` in its own process, not in the agents it spawns; verify). Belt
and braces: in `resolve_ownership`, ignore a monitor/proc id when `SASE_AGENT` is set, because
monitor/proc supervisors scrub `SASE_AGENT*`, so the two can only coexist through an agent
launch.

Found while researching `sase tool` enforcement and monitor wrapping
(research:202609/sase_tool_guard_and_monitor_wrap__cld.md).

task_type_fields.impact:
Every epic phase agent, the heaviest users of `sase tool run check`, silently loses compact
output (a large context cost per check) and retained logs, and its runs are misattributed. It
also blocks the proposed recipe guard and monitor wrapping: an inherited ownership or parent
variable would silently satisfy or distort both for every descendant agent.
task_type_fields.repro:
```bash
sase tool runs -a -A sase-135.7 -j | jq '.runs[] | {run_id, owner_kind, owner_id, logs}'
sase monitor list -a -j | jq '.monitors[] | select(.monitor_id=="136v0dbr3pv1") | {member_agent_name, command}'
```

Live repro: approve an epic, and in a phase agent run `sase tool run check`. The output streams
in full rather than compact, `sase tool show RUN -j` reports `owner_kind: monitor` with the
epic-launch monitor id, and `sase tool show RUN -l` has no retained output.
